questions.question: The foundation of Sanchi Stupa was laid by which of the following Kings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka**, the great Mauryan emperor, laid the foundation of the **Sanchi Stupa**.
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is one of the oldest stone structures in India and an important monument of Indian architecture.
 
• It was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• The Stupa is located in Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh, and is a **UNESCO World Heritage site**.
 
• The structure was built to house the relics of the Buddha and serves as a significant site for Buddhist pilgrimage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka** ruled the Maurya Dynasty from 268 to 232 BCE and is remembered for his role in spreading Buddhism across Asia.
 
• He embraced **Buddhism after the Kalinga War**, which prompted him to adopt a policy of non-violence and spiritual conquest.
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is an example of Ashoka's efforts to promote Buddhism and his patronage of Buddhist architecture.
 
• Inscriptions and carvings on the Sanchi Stupa provide valuable insights into the art, culture, and religious practices of ancient India.
 
• Ashoka's edicts, inscribed on pillars and rocks across the Indian subcontinent, emphasize moral and ethical conduct, non-violence, and religious tolerance.

questions.question: Megasthenes was an ambassador who was sent to the court of which Indian ruler by the Greek ruler, Seleucus Nicator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by **Seleucus Nicator** to the court of the Mauryan ruler, **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• He authored the famous historical account **‘Indica’**, which provides valuable insights into the Mauryan Empire and Indian society during that period.
 
• Megasthenes described the administrative system, social structure, economy, and culture of the Mauryan Empire in his works.
 
• The relationship between Seleucus Nicator and Chandragupta was formalized through a treaty, including a matrimonial alliance and territorial concessions to Chandragupta.
 
• Megasthenes’ writings are considered one of the earliest and most significant Greek accounts of ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the **Mauryan Empire** in ancient India (circa 321 BCE).
 
• Chandragupta unified most of the Indian subcontinent under his rule, creating one of the largest empires in Indian history.
 
• Under his reign, the Mauryan Empire established a centralized administrative structure and efficient governance.
 
 
 
• **Seleucus Nicator:**
 
 
• Seleucus I Nicator was a general under Alexander the Great and later established the Seleucid Empire.
 
• He ceded territories in modern-day Afghanistan and Pakistan to Chandragupta in exchange for 500 war elephants, which played a crucial role in his campaigns.
 
 
 
• **Indica by Megasthenes:**
 
 
• The book provides an account of Indian geography, society, religion, and governance.
 
• Although the original text is lost, fragments of it survive through later historians like Strabo, Arrian, and Diodorus.
 
 
 
• **The Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• It was one of the most powerful empires in ancient India and reached its zenith under Chandragupta’s grandson, Ashoka.
 
• The Mauryan administration was known for its efficient governance and detailed bureaucratic systems.

questions.question: How many Pillar Edicts or Major Pillar Edicts (PEs) of Ashoka are found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, inscribed **seven Major Pillar Edicts** during his reign.
 
• The Pillar Edicts were inscribed on massive stone pillars across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• These edicts primarily focus on **Dhamma (moral law)** and provide guidance on ethical and moral conduct.
 
• The Major Pillar Edicts address themes such as **non-violence, religious tolerance, and welfare of people and animals**.
 
• These inscriptions are written in **Brahmi script** and were meant to be easily understood by the common people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Locations of Major Pillar Edicts:**

 
 
• The Major Pillar Edicts are found at locations such as **Topra, Meerut, Kaushambi, Rampurva, Lauriya-Nandangarh, and Sanchi**.
 
 
 
• **Ashokan Inscriptions:**
 
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions are classified into **Major Rock Edicts, Minor Rock Edicts, Major Pillar Edicts, and Minor Pillar Edicts**.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script:**
 
 
• The Brahmi script, used in the edicts, is one of the earliest known scripts in India and was deciphered by **James Prinsep in 1837**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Edicts:**
 
 
• The edicts reflect Ashoka's commitment to **spreading Buddhist values** and his efforts to promote **peace and harmony** across his empire.
 
 
 
• **Material and Construction:**
 
 
• The pillars are made of **polished sandstone** and are considered architectural marvels of the Mauryan period.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first subcontinental empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mauryan Empire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mauryan Empire was established by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE after overthrowing the Nanda Dynasty.
 
• It is considered the first pan-Indian empire, which unified most of the Indian subcontinent under a single political entity.
 
• The empire reached its zenith under Emperor Ashoka, who promoted the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
• The Mauryan Empire's capital was Pataliputra (modern-day Patna), which became a center of administration and culture.
 
• The Arthashastra, an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy, is attributed to Chanakya, the advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• Founded the Mauryan Empire with the help of his mentor and advisor Chanakya (Kautilya).
 
• His reign marked the beginning of a centralized and bureaucratic administration.
 
 
 
• **Emperor Ashoka:**
 
 
• Considered one of India's greatest emperors, he ruled from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• After the Kalinga War, he embraced Buddhism and promoted non-violence and Dharma (moral law).
 
• Ashoka's edicts, inscribed on pillars and rocks, spread his message of Buddhism and ethical governance.
 
 
 
• **Arthashastra:**
 
 
• An ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
• Attributed to Chanakya, it provides insights into governance, administration, and diplomacy during the Mauryan era.
 
 
 
• **Administration:**
 
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly centralized, with the emperor at the apex of a hierarchical bureaucracy.
 
• Provinces were governed by royal princes, and a network of spies ensured the smooth functioning of the empire.

questions.question: Seleucus Nicator was a contemporary of ____________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chanakya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seleucus Nicator** was a **general of Alexander the Great** and later became a ruler, establishing the **Seleucid Empire**.
 
• He had **interactions with the Maurya Empire**, specifically during the reign of **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• **Chanakya** (also known as **Kautilya** or **Vishnugupta**) was the chief advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• Chanakya was instrumental in the formation of the **Maurya Empire** and played a key role in the defeat of the Nanda dynasty.
 
• He is also known for his work, the **Arthashastra**, which is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kanishka**__

 __
 
• **Kanishka** was a prominent ruler of the **Kushan Empire** in the 2nd century CE.
 
• He is known for his military, political, and spiritual achievements and for promoting the **Buddhist religion**.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**__
 __
 
• **Ashoka** was a famous emperor of the **Maurya Dynasty** in India, ruling from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• He is known for his conversion to **Buddhism** and his efforts to spread Buddhist principles across Asia.
 
 
 
• **Kalashoka**__
 
 
• **Kalashoka** was a ruler of the **Shishunaga dynasty** in ancient India.
 
• He is known for convening the **Second Buddhist Council** around 383 BCE.
